title: Condition cases
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Summer 1: Dealings with others and Important Lessons
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y9 lesson 34 (Pupil PDF worksheet: condition cases)
intro: Lesson 34: Important Lessons unit 6: the conditions of salah. To understand the nine conditions of salah listed by Ibn Baz and why each must be in place before we pray

questions.q: Explain why purity is a condition of salah. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: Allah does not accept a prayer without purification (Muslim); salah is standing before Allah, so body, clothes and place must be pure; Allah loves those who purify themselves (2:222).
questions.model: Point 1: the Prophet ﷺ made it a condition. Develop: 'Allah does not accept a prayer without purification' (Muslim). Point 2: respect for the meeting with Allah. Develop: 2:222, Allah loves those who purify themselves.

questions.q: How many conditions does Ibn Baz list?

Condition cases on the pupil PDF: eight cases (praying in a jumper with a stain of najasah unknowingly; praying Maghrib before sunset; a boy of twelve praying without wudu; praying towards the wrong direction after trying hard to find it; and four more). For each, valid or not, which condition, and what to do. Answer in the portal response box.
questions.a: Answers per the key, for example unknown najasah: valid (common view); Maghrib early: not valid, repeat; no wudu: not valid; wrong qiblah after effort: valid
questions.model: Teacher does case 2: 'Maghrib before sunset: not valid, because the time is a condition (4:103). Pray again after sunset.'

questions.q: what is the difference between a condition and a pillar?
questions.a: A condition is outside and before the salah (and lasts through it); a pillar is a part inside it

questions.q: Back to our ponder: how is salah like a key?
questions.a: Every condition must be right for it to be valid
